column1: # npm-pre-scan evaluation corpus — LEGITIMATE "PARENT" PACKAGES (benign controls)
# Purpose : the real, legitimate packages that the malicious names in
#           eval/corpus/real_malicious_holders.tsv imitate, plus a few popular
#           controls. Every flag raised here is a FALSE POSITIVE. This is the
#           only arm that can produce an FPR, and the dynamic subset produces
#           the project's first-ever measured Layer 2/3 false-positive rate.
# Source  : parents of the 2017 typosquat campaign + high-download packages from
#           data/top_packages.txt. Dependency counts and install hooks verified
# ============ EVERY ENTRY NOW CARRIES layers=0,1,2,3 (v21, item 8) ===========
# It used to be that only dependency-FREE packages could carry 2,3. The Layer
# dependencies could not be fetched: a dependency-bearing package failed its
# install (swallowed by `|| true`), `require()` then threw MODULE_NOT_FOUND
# (swallowed by the try/catch), and the layer produced an EMPTY behaviour
# profile that read as a clean PASS — a vacuous result, not evidence of
# precision. 16 of these 27 packages were capped at layers=0,1 for that reason,
# which is why the dynamic FPR was only ever measured over 11 of them.
# v21 vendors dependencies: they are resolved on the HOST with
# `npm install --ignore-scripts` and mounted read-only at /vendor, so the
# sandbox can load them without ever gaining network access. All 27 entries
# The `dyn_valid` safeguard has NOT been removed, only re-based: an entry is
# admissible to the dynamic denominators when its dependencies were actually
# supplied (`vendored`) or it never had any, AND no dynamic layer was killed by
# the wall clock. A package whose vendoring fails still falls out of those
# denominators rather than contributing a vacuous PASS.
